Pairs work when they CONTRAST a parameter axis (gl04 vs gl05 contrasts param-variation vs param-breakdown; gm01 vs gm02 contrasts constant vs varying radius; gm03 vs gm04 contrasts inside-cavity vs outside-obstacle). The cluster reading becomes a small theorem: each map names a position in a structured parameter space.

The gm-family (glass-meets-mould) cluster makes the integration-phase claim visible: form = body-physics + external-geometry. The gl-family already made the claim weaker (form = pin + gravity + body); the gm-family sharpens it by replacing pin+gravity with cavity-or-obstacle, which is a single object instead of two. gm03 (rounded-corner box) makes legible something gm01/gm02 hid - the cavity does not fully determine the vessel; the body's bending stiffness decides corner radius. So form is not 'cavity' alone but 'cavity x body-stiffness'. The corners are where the parameter shows itself.

gm04 (pressed onto sphere) inverts the topology: instead of body-in-cavity, form-in-body. This is the same body-physics, the same gravity, the same contact-projection - but the constraint geometry is OUTSIDE the body instead of INSIDE. The vessel that emerges (cloth draping over a sphere) shares the family signature with bottle-in-cylinder despite being topologically opposite. Crafts that match the gm-pattern (vacuum-forming, glass-slumping, draping in fashion, pottery on mandrel) similarly use either cavity OR master interchangeably - the same physical principle is at work and the simulation makes that principle explicit.
